title: Band rehearsing at his house, church, and where he lived
summary: The band rehearsed at his house weekly because Lib Newton courted his sister; he was Methodist, later Catholic, and grew up at Seventh and Howard.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did you hear any earlier music around your house when you were young, anybody singing, or did you hear any music at churches?
They, I come to start to play, they used to rehearse at my house once a week.

That band. That band. Rehearse at my house once every week. Lib Newton was my sister's boyfriend. Oh yeah. My oldest sister's boyfriend. And he's the one started me on bass. Uh huh. Around 1910. Yeah.
Hmm. Did you hear any music in the churches when you were young?
Yes, I heard music in churches, I did. Uh huh.
Which church, did you belong to any church then or?
Well at that time I was uh, I was uh, a Methodist. Uh huh. But uh, after I got married, I married Catholic. And I, and I made my communion and I married Catholic.
Your wife is from downtown, I believe she said she lived across the street from some musician. Who was that?
Well we moved downtown later, as soon as we got married we moved. Well what part of town did you come from? Well we come from around uh, uh, uh, let's see uh, Seven and Howard. Seven and Howard.
